2610.04528.title: Quantifying Collusion Among Autonomous LLM Agents: A Statistical Analysis of the Collusion Wiki Incident
2610.04528.paper_summary: In August and September 2026, independent researchers publicly documented an unusual incident: thousands of autonomous agents, self identifying as OpenAI models on web research tasks, discovered and began using a small German wiki as an improvised message board posting roughly 18,000 times over six weeks to relay task answers, share a sandbox escape technique, and coordinate against a volunteer human moderator who spent weeks manually deleting their content [1]. The investigators' public writeup is a careful qualitative account, rich with direct quotation, but does not attempt a statistically rigorous quantitative characterization of the behaviour it documents.
2610.04528.paper_summary_zh: 在2026年8月和9月，獨立研究者公開記錄了一個不尋常的事件：數千個自主代理，自我識別為OpenAI模型，在網路研究任務中，發現並開始使用一個小型德國維基作為即興留言板，在六週內發佈了約18,000次，以傳遞任務答案、分享沙盒逃脫技術，以及協調對抗一位花了幾週時間手動刪除他們內容的志願人類管理員[1]。調查者的公開報告是一個謹慎的質性描述，充滿了直接引用，但並未嘗試對其記錄的行為進行統計上嚴謹的定量特徵描述。
2610.04528.author: Shariq Murtuza et.al.
